[standards/itsm-operations/STD-OPS-CSDM-001-servicenow-csdm-adoption.md#11-purpose-statement]

### 1.1 Purpose Statement

This standard mandates the adoption and consistent use of the ServiceNow Common Services Data Model (CSDM) 5.0 framework for organizing, classifying, and relating all Configuration Items (CIs) within the enterprise CMDB. CSDM 5.0 provides a standardized, lifecycle-oriented approach to modeling IT services and their supporting infrastructure, enabling consistent service management practices aligned with ITIL 4 principles.

CSDM 5.0 establishes the canonical structure for representing business services, technical services, applications, and supporting infrastructure through seven integrated domains: **Foundation**, **Ideation & Strategy**, **Design & Planning**, **Build & Integration**, **Service Delivery**, **Service Consumption**, and **Manage Portfolios**. This framework enables effective service mapping, impact analysis, and IT service management while supporting modern cloud-native and hybrid environments. Adoption of this standard ensures all teams use consistent terminology, classifications, and relationships when populating and consuming CMDB data.
page_texts.6:
[standards/itsm-operations/STD-OPS-CSDM-001-servicenow-csdm-adoption.md#12-scope]

### 1.2 Scope

**In Scope:**

- All new CI records created in the ServiceNow CMDB
- All existing CI records subject to data remediation efforts
- All service mappings and business service definitions
- All application and application service registrations
- All technology management service definitions and relationships
- All CI relationships following CSDM patterns
- All discovery and integration processes that populate the CMDB
- CMDB health dashboards and compliance reporting

**Out of Scope:**

- Custom CI classes created for non-standard use cases (requires separate approval)
- Legacy data that has been formally exempted through the exceptions process
- Non-ServiceNow CMDB platforms (covered by separate standards)
- Operational data stored outside the CMDB (monitoring metrics, logs)
page_texts.7:
[standards/itsm-operations/STD-OPS-CSDM-001-servicenow-csdm-adoption.md#13-compliance-level]

### 1.3 Compliance Level

**MANDATORY** - All new service definitions, application registrations, and CI classifications must conform to CSDM standards. Existing CMDB data must be remediated to CSDM compliance within 18 months of this standard's approval. No new CI classes may be created outside the CSDM framework without formal ServiceNow Architecture Team approval.
page_texts.8:
[standards/itsm-operations/STD-OPS-CSDM-001-servicenow-csdm-adoption.md#14-business-rationale]

### 1.4 Business Rationale

The Common Services Data Model provides the foundation for successful IT Service Management by establishing clear relationships between business services, technology management services, applications, and infrastructure. Without a standardized data model, organizations suffer from:

| Challenge | Impact | Business Cost |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Inconsistent Service Definitions | Teams define "services" differently, causing confusion | Cannot accurately report on service health or availability |
| Missing Service Mappings | No visibility into what infrastructure supports which services | Impact analysis fails, leading to unexpected outages |
| Application vs. Application Service Confusion | Technical and business views of applications are conflated | Cannot differentiate development artifacts from runtime instances |
| Unclear Ownership | No consistent model for assigning service and technology ownership | Incident resolution delays, accountability gaps |
| Reporting Inconsistency | Every team structures data differently | No enterprise-wide service reporting or portfolio management |

**Benefits of CSDM Adoption:**

- **Common Language**: Customers with different roles, tools, and backgrounds appreciate the single page of CSDM showing how the data model covers different needs
- **Technical Debt Reduction**: Customers with bespoke, custom data models value not needing to maintain custom data models and functionality that supports them
- **Greater Out-of-Box Use**: ServiceNow products are architected and structured to create and use data in the way CSDM describes
- **Future-Proof**: As ServiceNow and partners add new functionality, CSDM will be the data model that will be used and expanded
- **Accurate Impact Analysis**: Clear relationships enable precise understanding of change and incident impact
- **Service Portfolio Visibility**: Executive dashboards showing service health, cost, and performance
- **ITIL Process Enablement**: CSDM directly supports incident, change, and problem management processes

[standards/itsm-operations/STD-OPS-CSDM-001-servicenow-csdm-adoption.md#15-csdm-key-principles]

### 1.5 CSDM Key Principles

CSDM was created based on key principles that guide decisions regarding entity names, definitions, and model implementation:

| Principle | Description |
| --- | --- |
| **Simplified Concepts** | Concepts are represented in a simple, distinct manner to eliminate duplicates and confusion over data sources |
| **Designed for Reporting & Analytics** | A prime objective of CSDM is to support consistent analysis |
| **Prescriptive Relationships** | The prescribed relationships and references should be leveraged as the main approach to link CSDM tables |
| **Shared Data Model Collaboration** | CSDM identifies a data model that is to be shared across products in support of simplified concepts and collaboration |
| **Definitions** | Agreed upon CSDM definitions should be used wherever the table, reference, or attribute is used |
| **CSDM OOB Tables** | Shared CSDM tables will be provided out of box on Z-boot or free app store plugin by default |
| **Consistent Data Integrations** | Leverage prescribed technologies when integrating external data sources to ensure data integrity |
| **CSDM Adoption** | Customer impacts per release will be limited by providing automation and guidance to accelerate CSDM adoption |
| **Data Governance & Process** | The presence of data in the model provides little value without governance and effective process to manage the veracity of the data |
| **Product Use Documentation** | Documented guidance on use and/or value of CSDM will be provided by each product team that references CSDM objects |

#### 2.2.0 CSDM Service Types

ServiceNow provides three OOB base-system service types that must be understood:

**Business Service**

A service type that is published to business users, typically underpinning one or more business capabilities as it provides specific value and outcomes.

- Business Services represent the highest value level in a CMDB
- A Business Service is how the customer sees the service being delivered, not what IT calls it
- Is an Operational CI (`cmdb_ci_service_business`), used for impact analysis in Incident, Problem, Change (IPC)
- Single Level; not a hierarchy

**Technology Management Service** (formerly Technical Service)

A service type that is published to service consumers, providing administrative and operational functions to manage technologies typically layered under Business and/or Application Services.

- Users can view and manage the technologies provided to the business (Provider focused)
- Event Management enables monitoring of service performance and identifies health issues
- Can be managed as part of the Service Portfolio
- Is an Operational CI (`cmdb_ci_service_technical`), used for impact analysis in IPC
- Single Level; not a hierarchy

**Service Instance** (Application Service and siblings)

A service type focused on the instantiation of a Service. CSDM 5 introduces several new Service Instance types beyond Application Services.

- May be designated by environment (Development, Test, Production, etc.)
- May be designated by region, line of business (LoB), or otherwise
- Is an Operational CI (`cmdb_ci_service_auto`), used for impact analysis in IPC
- Application Service Instances can be created through Manual Mapping, Service Mapping, Tags, or Dynamic Query
- New in CSDM 5: Data, Connection, Network, Facility, and Operational Process Service Instances

The following CI classes form the core of the CSDM and must be used consistently:
page_texts.15:
[standards/itsm-operations/STD-OPS-CSDM-001-servicenow-csdm-adoption.md#business-application-cmdbcibusinessapp]

##### Business Application (`cmdb_ci_business_app`)

Represents a design-time artifact that defines an application from a business and portfolio perspective. This is what appears in the application portfolio and represents the **logical application** independent of deployment.

| Attribute | Description | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Name | Portfolio application name | "Claims Management System" |
| Number | Unique application identifier | APP001234 |
| Operational Status | Lifecycle state | Operational, Development, Retired |
| IT Owner | Technical accountability | Enterprise Architect |
| Business Owner | Business accountability | Claims Director |
| Business Criticality | Impact classification | 1 - Critical, 2 - High, 3 - Medium |

[standards/itsm-operations/STD-OPS-CSDM-001-servicenow-csdm-adoption.md#product-model-cmdbciproductmodel---new-in-csdm-50]

##### Product Model (`cmdb_ci_product_model`) - **New in CSDM 5.0**

Represents a commercial or internal product that can be instantiated as services. Product Models define **what can be offered** before deployment.

| Attribute | Description | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Name | Product name | "ServiceNow ITSM" |
| Manufacturer | Product vendor | ServiceNow |
| Model Number | Version/SKU identifier | ITSM-PRO-2024 |
| Product Category | Classification | SaaS Application |

##### Software Model (`cmdb_ci_software_model`) - **Enhanced in CSDM 5.0**

Represents installable software at the design level, independent of any installation. Links to Software Instances in the Service Delivery domain.

| Attribute | Description | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Name | Software product name | "Oracle Database" |
| Version | Design version | 19c |
| Manufacturer | Software vendor | Oracle |
| Software Category | Classification | Database |

[standards/itsm-operations/STD-OPS-CSDM-001-servicenow-csdm-adoption.md#business-service-cmdbciservice]

##### Business Service (`cmdb_ci_service`)

Represents an IT-enabled business capability offered to consumers. Business Services describe **what** the business offers, not **how** it is delivered.

| Attribute | Description | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Name | Business-meaningful service name | "Claims Processing Service" |
| Service Classification | Category of service | Business Service |
| Operational Status | Current state | Operational, Retired, Pipeline |
| Service Owner | Accountable individual | Business Product Owner |
| Support Group | Team providing support | Claims Support Team |
| Business Criticality | Impact level | 1 - Critical |
page_texts.20:
[standards/itsm-operations/STD-OPS-CSDM-001-servicenow-csdm-adoption.md#application-service-cmdbciserviceauto]

##### Application Service (`cmdb_ci_service_auto`)

Represents a deployed, running instance of an application in a specific environment. This is the **runtime manifestation** of a Business Application.

| Attribute | Description | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Name | Environment-specific name | "Claims Management - Production" |
| Environment | Deployment environment reference | Production |
| Version | Deployed version | v2.3.1 |
| Business Application | Parent application (Design) | Claims Management System |
| Operational Status | Runtime state | Operational |
page_texts.21:
[standards/itsm-operations/STD-OPS-CSDM-001-servicenow-csdm-adoption.md#technology-management-service-cmdbciservicetechnical]

##### Technology Management Service (`cmdb_ci_service_technical`)

> **Note**: Technology Management Services were previously labeled "Technical Services" in CSDM 4 and before the Yokohama family release.

Represents a service type that is published to service consumers and provides the administrative and operational functions to manage the technologies that are typically layered under one or more Business and/or Application Services. Technology Management Services can be managed as part of the Service Portfolio.

| Attribute | Description | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Name | Service name | "Enterprise Oracle Database Service" |
| Service Classification | Technical Service | Database Service |
| Operational Status | Current state | Operational |
| Support Group | Operations team | Database Administration |
| Service Portfolio | Portfolio hierarchy reference | Infrastructure Services |
page_texts.22:
[standards/itsm-operations/STD-OPS-CSDM-001-servicenow-csdm-adoption.md#dynamic-ci-group-cmdbciquerybasedservice---new-in-csdm-50]

##### Dynamic CI Group (`cmdb_ci_query_based_service`) - **New in CSDM 5.0**

Represents a dynamically-defined group of CIs based on query criteria. Enables flexible service groupings that automatically update as infrastructure changes.

| Attribute | Description | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Name | Group name | "All Production Kubernetes Pods" |
| Query Definition | Filter criteria | Environment=Production AND Class=Container |
| Update Frequency | Refresh schedule | Real-time, Hourly, Daily |
| Purpose | Use case | Service Mapping, Impact Analysis |
page_texts.24:
[standards/itsm-operations/STD-OPS-CSDM-001-servicenow-csdm-adoption.md#environment-cmdbcienvironment---promoted-in-csdm-50]

##### Environment (`cmdb_ci_environment`) - **Promoted in CSDM 5.0**

Represents a deployment environment as a first-class CI, enabling better environment management and lifecycle tracking.

| Attribute | Description | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Name | Environment name | "Production - US East" |
| Environment Type | Classification | Production, Staging, Development, DR |
| Location | Physical/cloud location | AWS us-east-1 |
| Operational Status | Current state | Operational |

### 2.3 CSDM 5.0 Service Taxonomy

CSDM 5.0 emphasizes the distinction between **Design-time** (what we plan/build) and **Runtime** (what we operate) artifacts:

```text
CSDM 5.0 Artifact Hierarchy

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                DESIGN & PLANNING DOMAIN                     │
│  (Planning & Development - What we build)                   │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  Product Model ─► Software Model ─► Business Application    │
│  (Vendor product)  (Installable)    (Portfolio item)        │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                            │
                            │ Instantiated as
                            ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                SERVICE DELIVERY DOMAIN                      │
│  (Runtime Operations - What we run)                         │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  Business Service                                           │
│       │                                                     │
│       └─── Depends on ──► Application Service               │
│                                  │                          │
│                                  ├─► Technology Management Service      │
│                                  │        │                 │
│                                  └─► Infrastructure CIs     │
│                                           │                 │
│                                           └─► Dynamic CI    │
│                                                Groups       │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

**Classification Rules:**

| If the artifact... | Then classify as... | Domain |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Is a commercial/internal product definition | Product Model | Design & Planning |
| Is installable software at design level | Software Model | Design & Planning |
| Appears in the application portfolio | Business Application | Design & Planning |
| Delivers direct business value to end users | Business Service | Service Consumption |
| Is a deployed instance of an application | Application Service | Service Delivery |
| Provides shared technical infrastructure capability | Technology Management Service | Service Delivery |
| Is a dynamic grouping of CIs based on criteria | Dynamic CI Group | Service Delivery |

[standards/itsm-operations/STD-OPS-CSDM-001-servicenow-csdm-adoption.md#24-relationship-model]

### 2.4 Relationship Model

CSDM defines specific relationship types that must be used consistently. Configuration management is not effective without the use of relationships between CIs.

> **Note**: Several ServiceNow products (EA, Service Mapping, Discovery) have critical dependencies on these relationships. If these relationships are not used, functionality such as Technology Portfolio Management risk assessment will not function.

| Relationship | From CI Type | To CI Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Depends on::Used by` | Business Service | Application Service | Service depends on application |
| `Depends on::Used by` | Application Service | Technology Management Service | App uses technical service |
| `Depends on::Used by` | Application Service | Infrastructure CI | App runs on infrastructure |
| `Contains::Contained by` | Business Application | Application Service | App contains service instances |
| `Consumes::Provided by` | Business Application | Application Service | Portfolio to runtime |
| `Hosted on::Hosts` | Application Service | Server/Cluster | Where app is deployed |
| `Consumes::Consumed by` | Technology Management Service | Infrastructure CI | Service uses infrastructure |
| `Owned by::Owns` | User | Business Application | Ownership relationship |
| `Managed by::Manages` | Group | CI | Management responsibility |

**Relationship Hierarchy:**

```text
Business Service
    │
    └─── Depends on ──► Application Service (Production)
                            │
                            ├─── Depends on ──► Technology Management Service (Database)
                            │                       │
                            │                       └─── Runs on ──► Database Server
                            │
                            ├─── Runs on ──► Application Server Cluster
                            │
                            └─── Contained by ──► Business Application
```

#### 3.1.1 CI Classification Requirements

| ID | Requirement | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CSDM-REQ-001 | All services must be classified as Business Service, Technology Management Service, or Application Service | Enables consistent service reporting |
| CSDM-REQ-002 | All applications must have a Business Application record in the portfolio | Provides single source of truth for application inventory |
| CSDM-REQ-003 | All production deployments must have corresponding Application Service records | Enables runtime service mapping |
| CSDM-REQ-004 | All Business Services must be linked to supporting Application Services | Enables impact analysis |
| CSDM-REQ-005 | All Application Services must be linked to their Business Application parent | Maintains traceability from portfolio to operations |

| CSDM-REQ-007 | All services must have Operational Status accurately maintained | Supports portfolio management |

| CSDM-REQ-011 | All Business Services must have at least one dependency relationship | Services without dependencies provide no value |
| CSDM-REQ-012 | All Application Services must be linked to infrastructure CIs | Enables impact analysis |
| CSDM-REQ-013 | All relationships must use CSDM-approved relationship types | Maintains model consistency |
| CSDM-REQ-014 | Circular dependencies are prohibited | Prevents impact analysis failures |
| CSDM-REQ-015 | All Technology Management Services must document consuming Application Services | Shows service usage |

[standards/itsm-operations/STD-OPS-CSDM-001-servicenow-csdm-adoption.md#32-recommended-practices]

### 3.2 Recommended Practices

The following practices improve CSDM data quality and usability:

- **Service Criticality Assessment**: Classify all Business Services by business criticality (Critical, High, Medium, Low) to support prioritization
- **Service Level Documentation**: Link Service Level Agreements to Business Services for SLA management
- **Discovery Validation**: Validate automated discovery results before promoting to production CMDB
- **Regular Relationship Review**: Review and validate service relationships quarterly
- **Portfolio Rationalization**: Use Business Application records for application rationalization analysis
- **Change Impact Preview**: Test change impact analysis accuracy monthly using real changes
page_texts.33:
[standards/itsm-operations/STD-OPS-CSDM-001-servicenow-csdm-adoption.md#33-prohibited-practices]

### 3.3 Prohibited Practices

The following practices are explicitly prohibited:

| Prohibition | Rationale | Alternative |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Creating custom CI classes without approval | Fragments the data model | Use approved CSDM classes or request extension |
| Using "Generic Service" for all services | Prevents meaningful classification | Use specific service type classifications |
| Direct database updates bypassing IRE | Corrupts data quality | Use approved integration methods (see STD-OPS-CMDB-001) |
| Storing runtime data as configuration data | Confuses operational and configuration data | Use monitoring tools for runtime data |
| Creating Application Services without Business Application parent | Orphans application instances | Always create Business Application first |
| Using inconsistent naming conventions | Prevents searchability | Follow naming standards in Section 4.4 |
page_texts.34:
[standards/itsm-operations/STD-OPS-CSDM-001-servicenow-csdm-adoption.md#34-exceptions-process]

### 3.4 Exceptions Process

Exceptions to this standard require formal approval:

1. **Exception Request Submission**: Submit request via ServiceNow with business justification
2. **Architecture Review**: CMDB Data Architect reviews technical impact
3. **Governance Approval**: Configuration Management Advisory Board (CMAB) approves or denies
4. **Time-Bound Exceptions**: All exceptions have maximum 12-month duration
5. **Remediation Plan Required**: Exceptions must include plan to achieve compliance
6. **Quarterly Review**: All active exceptions reviewed quarterly for continued validity

#### Example 3: CSDM 5.0 Design-to-Operate Mapping (New)

**Context:** Demonstrating the CSDM 5.0 distinction between Design & Planning domain artifacts and Service Delivery domain runtime instances, including Dynamic CI Groups

**Implementation:**

```yaml
DESIGN & PLANNING DOMAIN (What we build):
──────────────────────────────
Product Model: "ServiceNow Platform"
├── Manufacturer: ServiceNow
├── Product Category: IT Service Management
│
└── Software Model: "ServiceNow ITSM Module"
    ├── Version: Washington DC
    │
    └── Business Application: "Enterprise ITSM Platform"
        ├── Number: APP002345
        ├── IT Owner: Platform Engineering Lead
        ├── Business Owner: VP IT Operations
        ├── Business Criticality: 1 - Critical
        └── Operational Status: Operational
                │
                │ Instantiated as
                ▼
SERVICE DELIVERY DOMAIN (What we run):
─────────────────────────────
Application Service: "ITSM Platform - Production"
├── Environment: Production (cmdb_ci_environment)
├── Version: Washington DC Patch 3
├── Operational Status: Operational
│
├── Dependencies:
│   ├── Technical Service: "ServiceNow Instance Infrastructure"
│   │   ├── Dynamic CI Group: "All ITSM MID Servers"
│   │   │   └── Query: class=MID Server AND application=ITSM
│   │   └── Hosted On: ServiceNow Cloud (US West)
│   │
│   └── Technical Service: "Enterprise SSO Service"
│       └── Hosted On: azure-ad-prod
│
└── Business Service: "IT Service Management"
    ├── Service Owner: IT Operations Director
    ├── Business Criticality: 1 - Critical
    └── Service Offerings:
        ├── Incident Management
        ├── Change Management
        └── Service Catalog
```

**CSDM 5.0 Key Concepts Demonstrated:**

- **Design-to-Operate traceability**: Business Application (Design) → Application Service (Operate)
- **Environment as CI**: Production environment is a proper CI reference, not just a text field
- **Dynamic CI Groups**: MID Servers grouped by query, automatically updated as infrastructure changes
- **Product Model hierarchy**: Vendor product → Software Model → Business Application

**Compliance Evidence:**

- Clear separation between design-time portfolio items and runtime services
- Environment CI properly referenced for all deployment instances
- Dynamic CI Groups used for infrastructure that changes frequently
- Full traceability from Business Service to supporting infrastructure
